newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Iran says has no oil for now to store in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Iran says has no oil for now to store in S.Africa.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said on Friday his government was still willing to discuss storing oil in South Africa, but had no reserves at present to set aside.

"I have commented in this regard in the past that we have no agreement reached over the matter and at present we have sold our oil in advance for several months, so there is no more oil to be stored," he told a news conference in Pretoria.
Rafsanjani was ending a two-day state visit to South Africa and met President Nelson Mandela for talks earlier.
"Should this matter be seriously demanded by the South Africans, maybe we could negotiate the matter over the next six months," Rafsanjani said.
He said that Iran's oil production quota was fixed by OPEC.
"It is not that we would be able to pump any amount of oil that we want out of our wells," he said.
Iran and South Africa began talks last year on using spare oil storage facilities at Saldanha Bay, north of Cape Town, for Iranian oil.
South Africa has spare capacity built up to protect against sanctions during apartheid, while Iran was said keen to find a safe storage facility away from the turbulent Gulf.
Washington has frowned on a possible deal.
"This matter will solely depend on South Africa," Rafsanjani said earlier.
"Should they find it to be in their interest, or the interest of the region, we would be available to sign an agreement to work that out."
